correctness.rationale: The free order-66 diagonal action, invariant elliptic fibre and zero section, and Kondō Picard lattice NS(S)=U give a primitive unimodular invariant summand of H²(S;Z). The holomorphic two-form has eigenvalue zeta^5 of primitive order 66; its degree-20 cyclotomic factor fills the rank-20 transcendental summand. Exact Phi_66(1)=1 makes (1-g*) invertible over Z on that summand, not merely over Q. Integral Wang sequence for the K3 mapping torus followed by Künneth with S¹ gives H^k(V;Z) free with ranks (1,2,3,4,3,2,1) and fundamental group Z². Invariant Hodge decomposition gives h^20=0, h^11=3 and h^21=2. Analytic exponential sequence with H²(O)=0, H³(Z)=Z⁴ implies zero cohomological torsion Brauer and thus zero Azumaya Brauer. Order-66 canonical bundle is topologically trivial because H²(Z) has no torsion. Exact sympy Phi_66 check was performed independently; no finite test stands in for Wang/lattice arguments.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality lies in the complete integral, torsion-sensitive cohomology and Brauer profile of the specific extremal quotient, not in constructing the quotient or determining NS(S). Singh explicitly constructs V^(3) with index 66 but does not state these integral groups or Brauer vanishing in the inspected text. Festi–Nijgh–Platt and Kondō supply the Picard input; Hashimoto–Kanazawa type-K quotients have K trivial and q=0, unlike this torsion-canonical quotient with q=1.
